title: Termwise equivalences induce equivalences of mapping simplices
statement: Use small simplicial sets and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] and coherent realization of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_n$ and $B_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow B_n$ be chains of small simplicial sets, and let maps $f_i:A_i\to B_i$ commute with all transition maps. For a chain $Z$, define $M(Z)_r=\coprod_{\alpha:[r]\to[n]}(Z_{\alpha(r)})_r$, with operators $(\alpha,z)\mapsto(\alpha\theta,t^Z_{\alpha(r),\alpha\theta(s)}\theta^*z)$ for $\theta:[s]\to[r]$, where $t^Z_{j,i}:Z_j\to Z_i$ is the chain composite. The induced simplicial map sends $(\alpha,a)$ to $(\alpha,f_{\alpha(r)}(a))$. If every $f_i$ is a categorical equivalence of simplicial sets, then the induced map of mapping simplices $M(A)\to M(B)$ is a categorical equivalence. Consequently, its coherent realization $\mathfrak C[M(A)]\to\mathfrak C[M(B)]$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence.

proof.text: For composable monotone maps $\theta:[s]\to[r]$ and $\psi:[t]\to[s]$, applying the two displayed operators gives the transition $t^Z_{\alpha\theta(s),\alpha\theta\psi(t)}t^Z_{\alpha(r),\alpha\theta(s)}=t^Z_{\alpha(r),\alpha\theta\psi(t)}$, followed by $(\theta\psi)^*$; simplicial transition maps commute with pullback. This is the operator for $\theta\psi$, and identity maps give identity operators. The ladder identities $f_i t^A_{j,i}=t^B_{j,i}f_j$ then show on each summand that $(\alpha,a)\mapsto(\alpha,f_{\alpha(r)}a)$ commutes with these operators. Thus the construction and its induced map are well-defined.

source.place: Section 3.2.2, mapping-simplex definition, printed p.179; Remark 3.2.2.5, functoriality.

proof.text: Induct on $n$, with the assertion for all commuting ladders of chains of length $n$. At $n=0$ there is exactly one map $[r]\to[0]$, and its last value is $0$. Hence $M(A)=A_0$, $M(B)=B_0$, and the induced map is the assumed categorical equivalence $f_0$.

source.place: Remark 3.2.2.5, induction on n, base case.

proof.text: For $n>0$ write $Z^-=(Z_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow Z_{n-1})$, $K_Z=Z_n\times\Delta^{n-1}$, and $P_Z=Z_n\times\Delta^n$, for $Z=A,B$. Map $P_Z$ to $M(Z)$ by $(z,\alpha)\mapsto(\alpha,t^Z_{n,\alpha(r)}z)$ in degree $r$. Its restriction to $K_Z$ lands in $M(Z^-)$. In the degreewise pushout $M(Z^-)\amalg_{K_Z}P_Z$, a pair with $\alpha(r)<n$ is identified with precisely this element of $M(Z^-)$, whereas the pairs with $\alpha(r)=n$ have no identifications and map identically to their summands in $M(Z)_r$. This gives a bijection in every degree. The operator formula in Step 1 shows that these bijections commute with pullback, including when a face changes the last value from $n$ to a smaller index. Thus $M(Z)=M(Z^-)\amalg_{K_Z}P_Z$ as simplicial sets. The ladder gives a commuting map of these spans with components $M(A^-)\to M(B^-)$, $f_n\times1_{\Delta^{n-1}}$, and $f_n\times1_{\Delta^n}$. The cofibration leg is $K_Z\to P_Z$, not the transition-induced leg into $M(Z^-)$.

source.place: Section 3.2.2 definition and Remark 3.2.2.5, explicit degreewise pushout calculation for the induction.

proof.text: The induction hypothesis makes $M(A^-)\to M(B^-)$ a categorical equivalence. By [lem-coef-joyal-homotopy-exponentials], the localized degreewise product, with its projections, is a product in the Joyal homotopy category. The two projection equations for $f_n\times1_T$ identify its localization with the product of the isomorphism represented by $f_n$ and the identity of $T$. Its inverse is the product of the inverse isomorphism and that identity, for $T=\Delta^{n-1},\Delta^n$. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] to the Joyal model category to conclude that these actual maps are categorical equivalences. By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], cofibrations are degreewise injections, so every simplicial set is cofibrant (its initial map is injective), and $K_Z\to P_Z$ is a cofibration (a product with the injective face inclusion). All six objects of the two spans are thus cofibrant, both displayed legs are cofibrations, and all three component maps are weak equivalences. Clause (b) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison] applies and proves that their pushout comparison, which Step 3 identifies with the specified map $M(A)\to M(B)$, is a categorical equivalence. This completes the induction without assuming any transition map injective.

source.place: Remark 3.2.2.5, induction using the one-cofibration pushout comparison; Corollary 2.2.5.4 for products.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ is the left adjoint in the Joyal--Bergner Quillen equivalence, hence preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. The weak-equivalence preservation clause of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] says that such a left adjoint preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects. Both mapping simplices are cofibrant because their maps from the empty simplicial set are degreewise injective, by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Apply this clause to the actual map proved weakly equivalent in Step 4. Its actual coherent realization is a Bergner weak equivalence, which is exactly a Dwyer--Kan equivalence by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison].

source.place: Coherent-realization consequence from Theorem 2.2.5.1 and the ordinary left Quillen preservation theorem.

proof_origin.place: Explicit expansion of the induction in HTT Remark 3.2.2.5, printed pp.179-180, read online; archive WANTED. Product and model-category inputs are cited as nodes.

The delivery is one commit containing only the item and its report, with no new nodes. Source check: HTT is not archived under literature/, so I fetched the primary PDF into /tmp. Its §3.2.2 definition on printed p.179 (simplex = monotone f:J→[n] with σ:Δ^J→A_{f(max J)}, operators (f∘p, e∘σ)) and Remark 3.2.2.5 on p.180 (ladder functoriality; termwise categorical equivalences give a categorical equivalence) match the item's statement exactly, with no hypothesis added or dropped. The coherent-realization clause is proved in Step 5. Steps: Step 1 checks operator composition and ladder naturality. Step 2 sets up the induction uniformly over all ladders, with n=0 giving f_0. Step 3: I recomputed the degreewise pushout M(Z^-)⊔_{Z_n×Δ^{n-1}} Z_n×Δ^n, where the complement of K in P is exactly the α with α(r)=n; it is a simplicial bijection and the map of spans commutes; no transition map needs to be injective. Step 4 combines four cited statements: the product in hsSet_J (joyal-homotopy-exponentials) plus localization detecting weak equivalences gives f_n×1 as an equivalence; all objects are Joyal-cofibrant and K→P is a cofibration (joyal-model-structure); clause (b) of model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison then applies, with every hypothesis checked and no properness needed. Step 5: coherent realization is left Quillen (coherent-nerve-comparison), so by the derived-adjunction preservation clause it preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects, and Bergner weak equivalences are Dwyer–Kan equivalences. Edge cases checked: n=0, n=1 (mapping cylinder), empty chains, an empty last fiber, constant chains, and non-injective transitions. Graph: proof_deps equals the union of the step uses; all six cited nodes are split, reviewed and in the same unit (sk-prop-sf-biduality-general), so no tool_uses are needed; the dependency closure is acyclic (435 nodes); there is no SGA. No base-change morphism or coefficient category is involved (not a target node). No fixes made.

lean.statement: theorem mapping_simplex_termwise_equivalence {n : ℕ} {A B : SimplexChain.{u} n} (f : A ⟶ B) (hf : ∀ (i : Fin (n + 1)) (C : SSet.{max u v}), C.Quasicategory → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map (f.app (op i)))).app C)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence) : (∀ (C : SSet.{max u v}), C.Quasicategory → ((hoFunctor.map ((MonoidalClosed.pre (uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map (mappingSimplexChainMap f))).app C)).toFunctor).IsEquivalence) ∧ DwyerKanEquivalence (A := CoherentNerve.underlying (Pinched.rigidification.obj (mappingSimplex A))) (B := CoherentNerve.underlying (Pinched.rigidification.obj (mappingSimplex B))) (Pinched.rigidification.map (mappingSimplexChainMap f))
